explanation: This is stalemate. It can rescue a player who is far behind, so a player with a big material lead has to take care to leave the opponent a legal move.

claims.text: In chess, when the player to move has no legal move and is not in check, the position is stalemate and the game is drawn.
Stalemate is neither a win nor a loss for either player, and a player may not pass a turn in chess.
Stalemate can save a player who is behind in material, so the stronger side must avoid leaving the opponent without a legal move.

evidence.restatement: Stalemate is a draw, not a win or loss, and chess has no passing.
Stalemate lets a side that is behind escape with a draw, so the stronger side must leave the opponent a legal move.
Under the FIDE Laws of Chess, a player with no legal move whose king is not in check is stalemated and the game is drawn.

issues.note: Historical rules differed (stalemate was a win for the stalemated side in shatranj, and a loss for the stalemating side in some older European rules). 'In chess' means the modern laws every player knows, so the key stands.
